body.v: Your October statement is attached as a PDF. You can also read it in the SwissAlpBank app, under Documents.
Replies to this address are not read.

hotspots.explain: The address is on swissalpbank.example, the bank's real domain, and there is no different reply-to.
A plain .pdf, not .pdf.html. The file type matches what the email says.
It says plainly that replies are not read, so nothing is sent to a strange address.
It tells you where to find the same statement yourself, in the app.

who.prompt: Who is really writing to you? Look at the address, not just the name.
who.answer: SwissAlpBank: the sender address is on the real domain and there is no reply-to pointing anywhere else.

emotion.prompt: What feeling is this email trying to create?
emotion.answer: None. It is routine mail with no deadline or threat.

ask.prompt: What exactly does it want you to do?
ask.answer: Nothing. It delivers your statement as a PDF. There is no sign-in, link or payment.
choices: Nothing: it only delivers a statement

verify.prompt: How can you check through a channel you control?
verify.answer: If you are unsure, open the SwissAlpBank app yourself and read the same statement there.
choices: Reply to ask for a paper copy
Forward it to a friend first

actions.label: Open the SwissAlpBank app yourself and read the statement there
actions.consequence: The same statement is there. You never needed the attachment.

actions.label: Open the PDF attachment
actions.consequence: It is a normal statement. A real .pdf from the real domain is fine to open.

actions.label: Reply to ask a question about the statement
actions.consequence: Nobody reads replies to this address. Use the app or the number on your card.

attacker_reveal: This one is real, dear. Same bank, same kind of attachment as the fake, but the file really is a PDF and nothing points to another address. Read file names to the end, and check the reply-to too.
